newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firmer as reserve levels ease off.
newsitem.headline: German call money firmer as reserve levels ease off.

text.p: German call money rates ticked up on Friday as the level of reserevs held at the Bundesbank eased back for the second session in a row.
Traders said rates were trading in a range of 3.00 to 3.05 percent, with main volumes trading at 3.02 to 3.03 percent, up from a 2.98 to 3.00 percent range on Thursday.

Data showing a pick up in M3 money supply growth in May in 7.0 percent from 6.7 percent in April gave the market little new direction, traders said, since it merely confirmed the view that interest rates were likely to remain on hold for the at least the medium term.
Some players said rates would remain at relatively firm levels, since the current somewhat lower reserve levels at the Bundesbank would remain in place until after the weekend.

Average daily reserve held at the central dropped to 38.9 billion marks on Thursday from Wednesday's already lower 39.9 percent level, while the monthly average eased back to 40.2 billion marks from 40.3 billion previously.
Borrowings on the Lombard facility were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA was at 3.04400 percent on Friday compared with 3.01800 previously.
